label: sequence started with digit 0 (late original phase through <DEL>)
explanation: Fires at steps t>=3 of the original phase and at the <DEL> step in sequences whose first original token is the digit 0 (first_tok=0 lift 21x, 93% of mass). Never active at t=0-2 and essentially silent during the copy phase (0.1% of mass), so it is a persistent memory of an initial 0 that turns off once output 0 is produced. Magnitude rises over the first few steps, peaking around t=4-6 (0.9-1.0 of max), then decays toward <DEL>; strongest when the sequence begins 0 0. Weak residual activations (about 7% of mass, lowest quartile) occur when 0 is the second token instead. It does not respond to the current input token identity.

issues: The main claims hold. On test the predicate scores P 0.995, R 0.704, F1 0.825, mass recall 0.931. Activity is zero at t=0-2, copy phase holds 0.08% of mass (P 0.0001), the original phase alone (t>=3) gets P 0.996 and mass 0.76, <DEL> gets P 0.991 and mass 0.18, mass peaks at t=4-5, and sequences starting '0 0' have the strongest examples (P 0.993).

There is a systematic miss class: sequences whose SECOND token is 0 (first token not 0). They account for 23% of all active steps (recall 0.23 on dev), though only 6% of mass. The explanation calls these weak scattered misses, but they follow a clear lag pattern: precision by step is 0.007 at t=3, 0.49 at t=4, 0.62 at t=5, 0.56 at t=6, 0.40 at t=7, 0.20 at t=8 and 0.21 at <DEL>. So the feature starts about 3 steps after the 0 whether the 0 is at position 0 or 1, and the onset delay is the same in both cases.

The previous agent tested orig(1)==0 without the time restriction. Its precision is diluted by t=3 (which is almost silent) and by t>=8/<DEL>, and that is why it got F1 0.78. With the window t=4-6 added, F1 improves on test.
A 0 elsewhere does not explain the remaining misses: with neither orig(0) nor orig(1) equal to 0, precision is 0.003. first_tok 'f' shows a small 1.5x lift but holds only 1% of mass, which is noise.

The phrase 'stored memory of an opening 0' overclaims a little. The feature is better described as a delayed signal for an early 0 (position 0 strongly, position 1 weakly, onset about 3 steps after the 0), not something tied strictly to the first token.
skeptic.revised_label: 0 among the first two original tokens; fires from about 3 steps after the 0 through <DEL> (strong when the 0 is first, weaker and limited to t≈4-6 when it is second)
